chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I mentioned something to Al-Reza (peace be upon him), so he said: 'Be patient, for I hope that Allah will do something for you, if Allah wills.' Then he said: 'By Allah, Allah does not delay from the believer in this world any good that He hastens for him in it.' Then he belittled the world and said: 'What is it?'

Then he said: 'The possessor of bounty is in danger, for it is obligatory upon him the rights of Allah in it. By Allah, if bounty comes upon me from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, I do not cease to be apprehensive about it, and he moved his hand until I take out the rights that are obligatory for Allah upon me regarding it.'
So I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, you are in your capacity and you fear this?' He said: 'Yes, so I praise my Lord for what He has favored me with.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual danger associated with receiving bounty according to Imam Al-Reza?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Reza (AS) elucidates the wisdom behind the delay of divine favors, asserting that what is postponed is often superior to what is hastened for the believer. He highlights the spiritual peril of wealth and status, noting that even the Imams remain in a state of *wajal* (reverential awe) regarding the fulfillment of Allah's rights, thereby modeling profound humility. This teaching underscores the concept that blessings are not merely gifts but trusts requiring diligent stewardship and gratitude.
